title: Puerto Rico: can you take a customer back from your partner?
seoTitle: Puerto Rico Law 75: taking accounts back or ending a dealer deal
description: A reserved exit clause may not settle a Puerto Rico dealer change. Understand the actual relationship before reallocating accounts, terminating or not renewing.
learningSummary: Before reclaiming a Puerto Rico account, consider what your local partner has built and undertaken to do. Law 75 can make that a dealer-relationship question even if the contract reserves an exit or direct-sales right.

sections.heading: Does Law 75 cover the relationship?
paragraphs: The reviewed Spanish consolidation includes real responsibility for distributing goods or providing services by concession or franchise in the Puerto Rico market. What the partner actually does matters more than the agreement’s label. Not every franchise, distributor or service partner is automatically a protected dealer.
Consider who develops customers, holds stock, hires people, provides service and invests locally. Those facts help establish the relationship to which the proposed change would apply.

sections.heading: What changes when you reclaim an account?
paragraphs: Article 2 addresses termination, impairment and nonrenewal without just cause, even where the contract reserves unilateral exit. Article 2A contains specific impairment presumptions and qualifications. These provisions do not make every change unlawful, but an expiry date alone does not settle the question.

Fictional example: an industrial-maintenance partner develops customers and employs technicians. After two years the brand wants its largest account back. Before reallocating it, establish who won and supported the customer, the reserved-account terms, investment, performance concerns and the exact proposed change. This example establishes neither protected status nor damages.
Review the agreement and proposed notice against that history, including any opportunity to correct performance. Statutory damages factors are not an automatic refund or a reliable damages forecast.

practicalOutput: Assess the proposed account or exit change against the actual dealer relationship before sending a notice.
limitations: Based on the Spanish government consolidation revised 13 November 2020; the English explanation is not an official translation. Later amendments and controlling cases remain unchecked.
Forum/arbitration wording must be assessed with applicable federal law; this does not invalidate every outside-Puerto-Rico arbitration clause.

Federal franchise duties apply to territorial franchises subject to exemptions. Independent sales, company and staffing questions remain separate; Puerto Rico’s inside-customs-boundary status does not settle product duties or territorial taxes.
editNote: Removed the repeated account quiz and change-file lecture; retained one account example and a direct relationship/change analysis.
conditionsRetained: Actual distribution/service responsibilities and conditional dealer status.
Article 2 just cause, unilateral-exit context and Article 2A qualifications.
No automatic damages or protected-account finding.
13 November 2020 Spanish text, later-authority and federal arbitration limits.
Territorial federal franchise scope/exemptions and limited customs finding.

title: U.S. Virgin Islands: what your operator needs from DLCA
seoTitle: USVI business licence: DLCA, tax clearance and regulated work
description: Check the local operator’s DLCA licensing, initial or renewal tax instructions, and any credentials needed for technical work.
learningSummary: For a first USVI business-licence application, DLCA lists tax clearance, police review and zoning, plus fire, health or professional reviews where applicable. Renewal has different tax-clearance instructions.

sections.heading: What DLCA checks
paragraphs: Use the local business’s legal name and any trading name, and identify its site on St. Thomas, St. Croix or St. John. Your brand agreement gives private brand rights; it does not complete the public licensing process.

DLCA’s instructions identify the following checks. The fire, health and professional requirements depend on the activity and location; this is not a requirement to visit every agency in one fixed order. Some checks are handled electronically on the applicant’s behalf.
bullets: Entity or trading-name registration and the appropriate business-licence category.
Initial tax clearance and police review.
Zoning and applicable fire or health review.
Applicable professional-board and personnel requirements for regulated work.

sections.heading: Is this a first application or a renewal?
paragraphs: DLCA lists tax clearance for an initial application. Its renewal instruction says a licence is issued without confirmation of tax clearance, while the business remains responsible for current tax obligations and possible later action. A renewal therefore does not establish that unpaid tax has disappeared.
Check the current filing destination: some links on the reviewed DLCA page are old.

sections.heading: Adding HVAC changes the question
paragraphs: Fictional example: a facilities partner plans cleaning and air-conditioning maintenance. DLCA lists mechanical/HVAC professions among its board-certification categories, so the actual technician tasks and applicable credentials need checking. Brand training does not establish a government qualification.
Describe the mechanical work before promising it to customers. Check the proposed site’s applicable reviews too, without assuming that every cleaning business needs a health inspection.

practicalOutput: Ask DLCA which licence category and site or professional reviews apply to the named operator’s proposed services.
limitations: DLCA operating licensing only; no approval of this business or its work is established.
The federal Franchise Rule includes territorial franchises subject to exemptions; independent territorial dealer/franchise law remains unresolved here.
USVI is outside the cited U.S. customs territory. Equipment and product shipments need their own route-specific review.
editNote: Replaced eight sections and two overlapping examples/tables with three owner-facing sections; the remaining example explains the HVAC complication rather than retesting the brand-licence distinction.
conditionsRetained: Actual local operator, island/site and activity determine the enquiry.
Applicable fire/health/professional reviews are conditional; electronic coordination and no universal agency order retained.
Initial tax clearance differs from renewal; tax liabilities/later action remain.
Current destination of old DLCA links is unverified.
HVAC board/personnel question is not settled by brand training; no automatic cleaning health inspection.
Federal territorial franchise scope/exemptions, unresolved independent local relationship law and outside-customs-boundary fact retained.

title: Guam: does the partner’s licence cover your company’s work?
seoTitle: Guam company authority and service-business licensing
description: Identify which company conducts Guam business and whether its actual services fall under general or separate trade licensing.
learningSummary: The Guam operator’s licence does not answer what your overseas parent or visiting technician may do. Start with each actor’s actual work, contracts and location.

sections.heading: When the foreign company needs authority
paragraphs: The cited provision requires a covered foreign corporation to obtain both a business licence and a certificate of authority before transacting business in Guam. Its listed exclusions matter: owning a subsidiary alone does not automatically mean the parent conducts the subsidiary’s business. The actual entity form and activities must be assessed.

sections.heading: Which services does the licence cover?
paragraphs: Chapter 76 describes an annual licence for covered non-professional service activity. It excludes services an employee provides to the employer, while section 76103 addresses services licensed under other provisions. Cleaning equipment, electrical repairs and engineering advice should therefore not be assumed to share one general-service route.
Describe the tasks to identify the relevant licence or profession. The Business License and Permit Center directory helps locate the office; it does not make every listed permit applicable.

sections.heading: Before promising the commissioning date
paragraphs: Fictional example: a Singapore brand trains a Guam partner and sends a manager to commission equipment. The partner hires technicians, stores parts and repairs systems. Check the parent’s own Guam activity, the operator’s service categories and any regulated work the visitor performs. Company authority does not establish professional credentials or the individual’s permission to work.

practicalOutput: Resolve the parent’s activity, the operator’s service categories and the visiting technician’s work permission before promising delivery.
limitations: Federal territorial franchise scope is subject to exemptions; independent Guam sales, relationship and tax requirements are not cleared here.
Guam is outside the cited U.S. customs territory. Product, origin, importer, actual route and quarantine questions need their own answer; no shipment charges or staffing approvals are established.
editNote: Replaced parallel explanations and actor-file choreography with three distinct questions and one short commissioning example.
conditionsRetained: Both business licence and certificate of authority before covered foreign-corporation transacting.
Entity/activity exclusions including subsidiary ownership alone.
Annual covered non-professional service category; employee-to-employer and separately licensed-service exclusions.
Separate trade/person work questions; no approved commissioning date.
Territorial franchise exemptions, independent local gaps and outside-customs-boundary scope.

title: CNMI: will a new service or island office need another licence?
seoTitle: CNMI business licence: additional activities and locations
description: CNMI’s rule ties general business licences to business lines and locations. Check a new site, rental activity or asset purchase before relying on an existing licence.
learningSummary: One company does not necessarily mean one CNMI business licence. The rule calls for a general licence for each business line at each Commonwealth location.

sections.heading: What an expansion changes
paragraphs: A licence is required before engaging in or continuing business. General licences last one year and are nontransferable. Fees are set by regulation; this guide verifies no amount. Other categories, including temporary events, have their own provisions.
Ask Finance how the actual activities and locations are classified. A company-registration or foreign-authority record from the Registrar does not replace the business licence.

sections.heading: Two offices and a new rental activity
paragraphs: Fictional example: a facilities partner proposes Saipan and Tinian offices plus equipment rental. Describe cleaning, maintenance and rental at each place for Finance’s classification. Do not turn that list into a confirmed licence count. Customer-site work also needs its actual location treatment established.
If the partner buys another operator’s equipment, the buyer must establish its own licensing: a nontransferable licence does not pass with the assets.

sections.heading: A licence does not provide the specialist
paragraphs: If an overseas technician is essential, investigate staffing before committing to a customer start. The described CW-1 route has employer, prevailing-wage, recruitment and labour-certification conditions; approved labour certification precedes the separate USCIS petition and is not itself work permission. The linked staffing guide explains this dependency.

practicalOutput: Ask Finance to classify the proposed business lines and locations before adding the service or site.
limitations: No customer-site classification, fee or licence set is approved. CW-1 availability and eligibility are not guaranteed, and the route does not authorise Guam/mainland work.

CNMI is outside the cited U.S. customs territory; imports/quarantine are route-specific. Federal franchise scope includes territories subject to exemptions; independent local sales, dealer, advertising and sector duties remain unresolved.
editNote: Removed the repeated grid exercise and management-output instructions; the site example now explains the licensing consequence once.
conditionsRetained: Before-business licensing, per-line/per-location rule, one-year term and nontransferability.
Finance classification, other licence categories and unverified regulatory fees.
Registrar/foreign-company records distinct from operating licence.
Customer-site treatment unconfirmed; asset purchase does not transfer licence.
CW-1 employer/wage/recruitment/certification-before-petition and individual work limits.
Territorial franchise/local-law and customs boundaries.

title: American Samoa: which company approvals come before trading?
seoTitle: American Samoa company permit and business licensing
description: Check the trading company’s permit, ownership-linked review and annual operating-licence calendar; visiting workers have a separate territorial route.
learningSummary: Identify the business that will sign local customers, employ staff and receive revenue. Its company permit and business licence are different questions, and the ownership structure can affect the review.

sections.heading: The foreign-corporation permit
paragraphs: The Attorney General’s checklist calls for certified company documents, corporate authorisation and resident-agent information for the covered foreign-corporation permit. It separately directs obtaining business licensing before transacting business. Domestic and nonprofit corporations are stated exceptions to that named foreign-corporation law; apply the rules for the actual entity form.

sections.heading: Ownership can change the review route
paragraphs: The official 2024 administrative compilation describes Territorial Planning Commission review linked to the applicant and ownership, plus a separate immigration-board policy for business-licence applicants classified as aliens under the applicable rules. Establish the actual ownership and control before selecting a route. The compilation must be read with statutory definitions and later changes; this page classifies no person’s status.

sections.heading: Know the business-licence calendar
paragraphs: Commerce says business licences expire at calendar-year end. It identifies October 1–December 31 renewal, post-January 1 late-fee treatment and January 31 suspension treatment. Check the current instructions against the issued licence.
A visiting trainer’s entry or work question follows the separate territorial process, not this renewal calendar. The companion guide explains what to resolve before arranging travel.

practicalOutput: Confirm the trading entity’s applicable permit, ownership review and issued business licence before starting local business.
limitations: The described territorial employment/family residency petitions require approval before entry; a mainland visa, ESTA assumption or company licence does not replace individual approval.

Federal franchise scope includes territories subject to exemptions; independent local sales/relationship law remains unresolved. American Samoa is outside the cited customs territory, with separate premises/import/quarantine questions.
editNote: Scoped to company, ownership and annual licensing. Replaced the repeated visiting-trainer story with a short linked note.
conditionsRetained: Foreign-corporation checklist and entity-specific domestic/nonprofit exceptions.
Business licensing before trading; actual operator distinguished.
2024 compilation, applicant/ownership review and no status determination.
Year-end expiry, October–December renewal, January late/suspension distinctions.
Separate pre-entry individual process and territorial customs/franchise limits.

title: Shipping to a U.S. territory: is it inside the customs boundary?
seoTitle: U.S. territories customs boundary: Puerto Rico, Guam and USVI
description: Find the five territories’ boundary status, then check the actual product and journey before relying on a freight quote or copied import calculation.
learningSummary: Puerto Rico is inside the cited U.S. customs territory; Guam, CNMI, American Samoa and USVI are outside it. That answers a boundary question, not the duty or total cost of a shipment.

sections.heading: The five destination answers
paragraphs: The federal definition covers the states, District of Columbia and Puerto Rico. Read the table only within that definition: “inside” does not mean tax-free, and “outside” does not supply a tariff or entry permission.

sections.heading: Before approving the equipment order
paragraphs: Fictional example: a Dutch brand copies its Puerto Rico equipment-cost sheet for Guam and changes only the address. The customs assumption no longer matches, and neither destination’s boundary status supplies the missing product treatment or charges.

Establish the product, manufacturer/origin, intended use, classification, exporting party, importer, receiver, port and any onward journey. Local taxes, product controls, quarantine and federal overlays depend on the actual route and goods. A later territory-to-mainland shipment has its own treatment.

Keep legal duties/taxes distinct from freight, broker and storage quotes. A contingency funds uncertainty; it does not establish an unknown legal charge. A freight price alone is not a complete landed-cost calculation.

practicalOutput: Obtain the product- and route-specific entry and charge answers before treating a shipping quote as landed cost.
limitations: No tariff, tax amount, product-entry permission or onward-shipment treatment is determined here.
editNote: Replaced two overlapping tables and a repeated shipment quiz with one boundary table and the commercial costing consequence.
conditionsRetained: States/DC/Puerto Rico inside; other four named territories outside under the cited definition.
No inside-equals-tax-free or outside-equals-tariff inference.
Product/origin/classification/importer/port/intended-use/onward-route variables.
Territorial tax, controls/quarantine and applicable federal overlays unverified.
Legal charges distinct from commercial quotes/contingency; no landed-cost figure.

title: CNMI CW-1 staffing: can the technician start when you need them?
seoTitle: CNMI CW-1 labour certification and worker start dates
description: Labour certification is not permission to work. Check the actual employer, job and immigration stage before committing to a technician-dependent customer start.
learningSummary: A technician agreeing to travel does not establish a lawful start date. CW-1 is a particular CNMI employment route with employer and labour steps before a separate USCIS petition.

sections.heading: Start with the actual employer and job
paragraphs: DOL describes conditions including a physical CNMI business location, an employer relationship and a Federal Employer Identification Number. The actual duties, worksite, supervisor, proposed wage and hiring entity matter; the overseas brand’s need for help does not establish eligibility.
Consider a locally recruited manager and an overseas specialist separately. The route cannot be selected from the title technician alone.

sections.heading: The labour and immigration stages
paragraphs: The reviewed DOL process includes a prevailing-wage determination, required U.S.-worker recruitment and temporary labour certification. Approved labour certification must precede the separate petition to U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS).

An application, recruitment record or approved labour certification alone is not permission for the person to work. Establish the separate current approval and status needed for employment before relying on the start date.

sections.heading: If the customer date comes first
paragraphs: If the essential specialist’s route remains unresolved, reconsider staffing, the promised scope or the customer date. Cost the supported wage, benefits, employer-paid obligations and recruitment/timing assumptions rather than copying a mainland staffing estimate or entering an unknown charge as zero. Keep personal immigration documents in the authorised private process.

practicalOutput: Resolve the essential technician’s actual employer/job route and work permission before promising the customer start date.
limitations: No occupation code, cap availability, employer/individual eligibility or approval date is established. CW-1 is not general authority to work in Guam or the mainland.
editNote: Removed both overlapping approval tables and the repeated pilot exercise; retained the critical labour-versus-work-permission dependency.
conditionsRetained: Physical CNMI employer/location, FEIN and actual job/worksite conditions.
Prevailing wage, required recruitment and approved labour certification before USCIS petition.
Certification/application alone not work permission; status still required.
No cap/eligibility/code prediction or Guam/mainland portability.
Supported process costs and private immigration-document handling.

title: Sending a trainer to American Samoa: check the work before booking
seoTitle: American Samoa visiting trainer entry and work approval
description: A short training trip can include live customer work. Check the territorial route for the actual person and duties before relying on a mainland travel assumption.
learningSummary: American Samoa has its own entry and residency arrangements. A four-week training label, overseas employment or a company business licence does not establish permission for the proposed visit and work.

sections.heading: What must be settled before entry?
paragraphs: Legal Affairs describes separate visitor and residency routes. The employment- and family-based residency petitions described in its instructions must be completed and approved before entry. The applicable route depends on the person and intended activities.

A mainland U.S. visa or ESTA assumption cannot be substituted for the territorial answer. Use the person’s actual nationality/status facts, dates, locations and local employer or sponsor through the authorised process; keep passports and applications private.

sections.heading: Training can include operational work
paragraphs: Fictional example: a visiting supervisor teaches procedures but also directs crews on live contracts and resolves customer problems. Describe those duties rather than relying on the short itinerary. This guide does not classify the trip as permitted or prohibited.
If the required person cannot lawfully start in time, choose a supported staffing alternative, reduce the service scope or reconsider the launch date before making customer promises.

practicalOutput: Obtain the person-specific territorial answer for the actual duties before booking essential travel or promising their work.
limitations: The business licence has a separate calendar: year-end expiry, October 1–December 31 renewal and distinct late-fee/suspension treatment. Neither the company’s renewal nor an individual approval replaces the other.
editNote: Removed the duplicated four-week quiz and detailed company-calendar diversion; retained one example of training becoming live work.
conditionsRetained: Distinct territorial visitor/residency routes and person/activity conditions.
Described employment/family petitions approved before entry; mainland visa/ESTA/company licence insufficient.
No trip approval or prohibition finding.
Private documents outside the educational site.
Separate business renewal calendar retained briefly.

title: Pittsburgh: does an outside service business need to register?
seoTitle: Pittsburgh business registration for outside service companies
description: Customer-site work inside Pittsburgh can matter even without a city office. Check the actual commencement date and Finance verification.
learningSummary: An office outside Pittsburgh does not close the registration question if your business performs work or services wholly or partly inside the city.

sections.heading: Check the work and commencement facts
paragraphs: The published city process includes outside businesses performing that city work. Identify the actual service address and start facts. The page quotes a 15-day registration provision; apply it to the relevant commencement event rather than guessing a deadline from incorporation or contract signing.

sections.heading: Submission is not completion
paragraphs: The city says registration is not complete until Finance issues verification. Ask for that confirmation after following the applicable process; a payment, account reference or submitted form is not the verification itself.
A depot’s premises use or regulated service still has its own requirements. City registration does not classify the brand agreement or complete franchise-sales disclosure.

practicalOutput: Check the actual Pittsburgh commencement event and obtain Finance’s registration verification.
limitations: The reviewed process does not establish every premises, sector or other obligation, or current fees. No unsupported date calculation is supplied.
editNote: Reduced six sections to the outside-work trigger and the separate completion event; removed the repeated cleaning story and register tutorial.
conditionsRetained: Outside business performing work/services wholly or partly in Pittsburgh.

title: Atlanta: why a paid tax application can still be unfinished
seoTitle: Atlanta occupation-tax certificate and zoning review
description: ATLBIZ and Accela handle different Atlanta tasks. Check zoning and the issued certificate before treating a paid application as finished.
learningSummary: Paying the occupation-tax application charge does not establish that Atlanta has issued the certificate or completed the proposed location’s zoning review.

sections.heading: Which task is in which system?
paragraphs: The ATL311 instructions distinguish the occupation-tax application in ATLBIZ from location zoning review through Accela. Applicable regulatory permits depend on the activity. Describe the real proposed use, including storage, equipment or customer visits, rather than simply services.

sections.heading: What remains after payment?
paragraphs: The instructions describe issuance after required documents and payment. If the tax application is paid but zoning remains unfinished, obtain the missing location answer and the actual issued certificate; opening another account or paying again does not answer zoning.
Use the same legal business, activity and address throughout. Tie the opening commitment to the applicable approvals, not an account screen or a processing estimate.

practicalOutput: Confirm the Accela zoning outcome and issued occupation-tax certificate for the actual site and activity.
limitations: No universal permit list, fixed agency order, complete tax/employment/franchise review or guaranteed opening date is provided.
editNote: Replaced the repeated portal exercise and document-role instructions with the two systems and the payment-to-issuance distinction.

Actual entity/activity/address and applicable regulatory permits.

title: City of Miami: which use and tax records does the site need?
seoTitle: City of Miami Certificate of Use and city/county tax receipts

learningSummary: Check the premises’ municipality before using a Miami-area application. A City of Miami depot is not governed solely by instructions for unincorporated Miami-Dade.

sections.heading: The address selects the local enquiry
paragraphs: Use the exact site and actual operator. A postal label or county-wide customer territory does not determine whether the premises are inside City of Miami boundaries.

sections.heading: The three records to distinguish
paragraphs: The city generally places its Certificate of Use before the city Business Tax Receipt, with stated exceptions. Check whether that use requirement or an exception fits the actual business. The city also directs businesses to a separate Miami-Dade County tax receipt.

rows: City Certificate of Use or applicable exception
The city’s premises-use requirement for the actual proposal
The City of Miami business-tax process

sections.heading: Do not close the site question with one receipt
paragraphs: For a depot storing equipment and dispatching teams, describe that use when obtaining the city answer. A county receipt does not demonstrate that the city use decision or city tax process is complete. Any separate trade, health or fire review depends on the actual activity.

practicalOutput: Confirm the site’s municipality, then resolve the city use requirement or exception and both tax-receipt processes.
limitations: Unincorporated-county sites need their applicable route. Fees, additional activity permissions and a complete opening or franchise-sales clearance are not established here.

seoTitle: Jacksonville tax receipt and Certificate of Use

learningSummary: A Local Business Tax Receipt and a Certificate of Use answer different questions. Receiving the tax receipt does not, by itself, settle whether the proposed commercial premises can be used as planned.

sections.heading: What the tax receipt leaves open
paragraphs: The reviewed city guidance calls for the local tax receipt before covered business. It identifies a separate Certificate of Use process for a new or expanding commercial operation. Check the requirements for the actual activity and site rather than assuming whichever document arrives first completes the opening.
For a depot, describe what happens there, including storage or other proposed work, and obtain the applicable use answer. An application or payment is not an issued use record.

sections.heading: Check the municipality for each operation
paragraphs: The city instructions identify additional municipal tax routes for the beach municipalities and Baldwin. A second operation in Jacksonville Beach therefore needs its own local-tax enquiry; the first depot’s receipt does not answer it.
Use the exact operating address. A wider service territory called Jacksonville does not identify the local government responsible for every location.

practicalOutput: Confirm the depot’s Certificate of Use requirement and obtain the applicable municipal tax answer for any additional operation.
limitations: The reviewed tax/use process does not settle every premises, professional, employment, tax or franchise-sales requirement. Fees and a universal approval sequence are not established.

learningSummary: For a Kansas City, Missouri workshop, the city business licence is only one question. The proposed address use and any regulated trade have to be considered too.

sections.heading: Check the KCMO site and proposed use
paragraphs: The reviewed BizCare guide identifies zoning clearance for a new business with a KCMO address and for address changes. Describe storage, workshop work, equipment, customer access and any trade activity so the location enquiry concerns the actual proposal.

paragraphs: BizCare distinguishes city registration/licensing and additional industry requirements, and acknowledges state-law exemptions. Establish whether an actual exemption fits rather than treating the general guide as one identical licence duty for every service.

If the workshop operator will perform a regulated construction trade, obtain that activity-specific answer as well as the location and city business outcomes. A completed online account is not licence issuance.

title: Baltimore City: who handles the business licence?
seoTitle: Baltimore City business licence clerk versus Maryland tax account
description: A Maryland sales-tax account does not settle a Baltimore City licence category. Check the actual activity with the correct City clerk.
learningSummary: Baltimore City and Baltimore County are different jurisdictions. For a City business, a County contact list and an existing Maryland tax account do not establish the applicable City business licence.

sections.heading: The tax authority and licence clerk have different jobs
paragraphs: Maryland’s Comptroller separates sales/use-tax registration from licence categories handled through the Clerk of Circuit Court. The applicable licences are issued for the county or Baltimore City where the business is located. Here the clerk is performing a licensing function, not handling a lawsuit.
The actual goods and services determine which category needs investigation; not every service business needs every clerk licence.

sections.heading: Adding equipment sales can change the enquiry
paragraphs: For a City workshop adding equipment sales to servicing, give the City clerk the exact address, legal business and mix of sales/services. The state sales-tax account remains relevant to its own process but does not answer the clerk category. Premises use and professional qualifications require their applicable answers too.

practicalOutput: Ask the Baltimore City clerk which licence category fits the proposed sales/service activity.

title: Houston: check the unit’s permitted use before committing rent
seoTitle: Houston commercial lease: Certificate of Occupancy and use
description: Request the occupancy record for the exact Houston unit and compare your proposed work before relying on a landlord’s commercial-space description.
learningSummary: A bay previously used by a business is not necessarily suitable for your planned storage, equipment or customer access. Establish the actual City of Houston unit and its authorised use before building a lease or opening date around it.

sections.heading: What the reviewed city guidance establishes
paragraphs: The city business page says a Certificate of Occupancy (CO) is required before a commercial building or individual lease space is occupied, or when its occupancy classification changes. Obtain the current record and compare it with the proposed activities, layout and alterations.
Describe relevant storage, chemicals, powered equipment and public access. The city lists building, fire, food and other reviews, but that does not make every permit mandatory for every business.

paragraphs: Check the parcel, address and unit: the Houston metro, Harris County and City of Houston are not interchangeable. A mailing address or landlord’s account of the previous tenant does not settle the responsible authority or proposed use.

Resolve the applicable occupancy and inspection questions before relying on the date at which rent, equipment orders or customer promises create costs. You may model a delay to understand exposure, but it is not the city’s promised timetable or a legally required lease clause.

practicalOutput: Obtain the exact unit’s current CO and ask which approvals your proposed use requires before relying on the lease/opening plan.

title: NYC: which building document supports your proposed use?
seoTitle: NYC CO, TCO, LNO and Letter of Completion explained
description: Identify the purpose of the New York building document in hand before treating it as permission for the business you plan to operate.
learningSummary: A completed building job and permission for your proposed use are different questions. Identify the actual document, property and unit before relying on the landlord’s records.

sections.heading: What each document can establish
paragraphs: A Certificate of Occupancy (CO) establishes legal use or occupancy. New buildings need one, and relevant changes to use, occupancy or egress—the ways people leave—can require a new or amended CO.

rows: Legal use or occupancy; compare the proposed activity with the actual record.
Temporary permission, not a final CO.
Legal-use confirmation under its applicable conditions; not a universal CO substitute.
Qualifying completed work that did not require a new or amended CO; not an LNO or blanket approval of the next use.

sections.heading: The pre-1938 exception is conditional
paragraphs: Certain lawful pre-1938 buildings may have no CO unless later changes triggered the requirement. Age alone does not establish the position.

For an old office proposed for training, identify whether the supplied completion letter is actually the relevant DOB record and what work it covers. Then compare the intended classes, occupancy and alterations with the legal-use evidence; this does not calculate capacity or approve the proposal.

sections.heading: Where to look for CO requests
paragraphs: For CO requests before March 1, 2021, DOB directs users to BIS; for requests on or after that date, to DOB NOW. The cutoff concerns CO requests, not every kind of building record. Check the relevant property records for open applications, violations and required sign-offs as well as the certificate or letter.

practicalOutput: Identify the actual building document and confirm that its use and conditions fit the proposed operation.
limitations: NYC DOB occupancy records only; no property, capacity, lease, fire, accessibility, sector or licence approval is supplied.
editNote: Moved one document comparison to the answer and removed the repeated old-office quiz and duplicate document-purpose-table task.
conditionsRetained: CO versus temporary CO, LNO and qualifying Letter of Completion purposes.
New building and relevant use/occupancy/egress change conditions.
Lawful pre-1938 route conditional on later triggers.
Contractor letter identity not assumed to be DOB document.
March 1, 2021 cutoff limited to CO-request systems.
Open records/sign-offs and no actual use/capacity clearance.

title: Buying a San Jose café: check the buyer’s permit before spending
seoTitle: San Jose café takeover: new-owner food permit and changes
description: A seller’s food permit does not transfer. Use Santa Clara County’s pre-purchase evaluation and describe menu or equipment changes before committing to fit-out.
learningSummary: An operating café still needs a new-owner permit answer when you buy it. Santa Clara County offers evaluation before purchase, which can expose further review before you commit to equipment or fit-out.

sections.heading: The seller’s permit cannot pass to you
paragraphs: For the fixed retail food process discussed here, the county requires a facility evaluation for takeover and the new operator’s own health permit before operating. Identify the actual buyer/operator and ownership-change date.

SCCDineOut provides historical inspection observations and closure information. That history can help investigate the facility, but an old score or placard does not transfer the permit or approve your menu.

sections.heading: A changed menu or kitchen can require further review
paragraphs: The October 2026 evaluation packet asks about food preparation, menu, equipment and remodelling; provide the menu where preparation occurs. Changed menus, new equipment or major structural deficiencies can lead to plan review.

If you retain a café counter but add hot-food cooking and equipment, describe the new process and hood arrangements before budgeting only for evaluation. The plan route asks for the actual scope, equipment/specifications, finishes and relevant mechanical/plumbing/electrical information. A complete submission and payment enter the review queue, not approval. Approved plans, relevant construction inspections and operating-permit steps remain different stages.

sections.heading: Before the nonrefundable fit-out deposit
paragraphs: Obtain the county’s route for the actual changes and the separate city building/use/fire answers for the planned works. Specialised processes, including reduced-oxygen packaging or manufacturing, need their applicable review rather than automatic use of the ordinary takeover route.

practicalOutput: Use the county evaluation before purchase and resolve the proposed menu/equipment changes before committing to fit-out.
limitations: County fixed-food process only. San Jose tax/zoning/building/fire pages were inaccessible, so no city fee, exemption, deadline or premises outcome is established.
No numeric current fee, guaranteed review duration or actual operating approval is supplied.
editNote: Replaced the duplicated café exercise and five-role task table with the purchase, changed-kitchen and spending decisions.
conditionsRetained: Nontransferable permit, facility evaluation and new permit before operating.
Pre-purchase evaluation and actual ownership-change/operator facts.
October 2026 packet, menu/prep/equipment/remodelling and change-dependent plan review.
Complete file/payment before queue; plans, construction inspections and permit distinct.
Inspection history and special processes limited to their actual uses.
City-source access gap, unknown fees/timing and no site approval.

title: Indianapolis extinguisher work: the company and each person need checking
seoTitle: Indianapolis extinguisher company and service-person licences
description: Check the local business and each extinguisher technician’s licensing and certification; the workshop’s construction-completion question is separate.
learningSummary: Do not dispatch the whole team on the strength of one company document or one technician’s credentials. The reviewed Indianapolis process identifies both the business and each service person.

sections.heading: The named service needs both checks
paragraphs: The city guidance calls for a business licence and each service person’s licence for the named fire-prevention equipment service. Individual applications also need the Indianapolis Fire Department’s certification stamp. The linked forms concern fire-extinguisher servicing, not automatic permission for alarms, sprinklers, sales, installation or every maintenance task.

The company and individual applications identify the actual local business and associated person. Brand training or the overseas parent’s licence does not establish those permissions. The city’s current published page still links applications marked October 2023. Confirm the applicable fees, certification steps and licence terms; the separate signed 2026 premises letter does not update those licensing terms.

sections.heading: If the workshop also has construction work
paragraphs: The signed 2026 city/county letter says it does not currently issue a Certificate of Occupancy. For covered construction it describes the permit holder’s Certificate of Completion and Compliance within 14 days after completion AND before occupancy or use. Those are both conditions, not 14 days in which opening is allowed.

A stated structural-permit exception depends on a registered architect or engineer properly filing the specified certificate. The separate fee trigger 30 days after permit expiry is not an opening grace period. Check whether the actual parcel is in the consolidated jurisdiction or an excluded municipality.

practicalOutput: Confirm the correct company permission and each proposed technician’s certification/licence before offering the named extinguisher service.
limitations: Administrative guidance and dated linked forms only; current ordinance scope, insurance/storage/environmental requirements and work outside Indianapolis remain unchecked.
The premises letter concerns 2026; current fee/renewal terms, actual permit exception and excluded-municipality boundary remain unresolved.
editNote: Removed repeated cleaning/two-technician stories and roster instructions; the construction letter is now a clearly separate short condition, not the main licensing narrative. Source follow-up: The company/person licensing answer and construction-completion answer are distinct and remain separated in the replacement. Published current links were confirmed, but the form revision dates remain October 2023. This is not verification of a new 2026 licensing fee, renewal schedule or complete ordinance scope.
conditionsRetained: Business AND each service person; Fire Department stamp.
Actual company/person identification and extinguisher-only form scope.
October 2023 forms do not verify current fee/renewal terms.
2026 completion within 14 days AND before use; structural-permit filer exception.
30-day-post-expiry fee not occupancy grace; actual jurisdiction exclusions unverified.

Source follow-up scope: Current ordinance/application scope beyond the named extinguisher work Current fees, licence duration, renewal/certification detail and actual worker/company status Actual parcel jurisdiction and whether the stated structural-permit exception applies

title: Detroit food businesses: what the removed licence did not change
seoTitle: Detroit BSEED licence change and retained food-health duties
description: The July 2025 change removed named BSEED licences, not the Health licence or applicable food-project and preopening requirements.
learningSummary: Detroit’s dated notice is not a general licence-free opening rule. Establish which food authority and project requirements fit the operation you plan to run.

sections.heading: Which licence changed?
paragraphs: The 16 July 2025 notice names restaurants, restaurants with a Michigan Liquor Control Commission licence, bar class C, mobile food vendors and coffee houses as no longer needing the named BSEED licence. It expressly retains a Detroit Health Department licence. Other food, premises or alcohol permissions are not removed by that statement.

sections.heading: Which food authority handles the operation?
paragraphs: Michigan guidance sends establishments primarily serving food for immediate consumption to the local health department, and businesses primarily selling, storing or manufacturing food to MDARD. Describe mixed activity, separately operated preparation, seating, mobile work or manufacturing rather than choosing a route from a grocery or coffee label.

sections.heading: What changes when you prepare or remodel the space?
paragraphs: Section 289.6103 exempts temporary food establishments and retail groceries from the specified plan-review requirement, with qualifications for food service in a grocery and a distinction for a grocery deli with customer seating. A plan exception is not a licence exemption.

Submitted plans need the section 289.6105 transmittal identifying the project and owner, operator or designated agent, with required fees; inaccurate or incomplete information can cause rejection. After covered construction, alteration, conversion or remodelling, section 289.6115 requires completion notification, a licence application and a preopening evaluation before opening. The local department may set the request lead time.

For a coffee shop adding preparation and seating, obtain the actual plan-applicability and Health opening answers before serving. The removed BSEED item or possession of the finished shop does not complete those steps.

practicalOutput: Confirm the actual food authority, plan requirement or exception and applicable Health opening steps before serving.
limitations: The longer local opening, premises and direct Health instructions were inaccessible. Current local forms, fees, renewal/inspection timing, zoning and building/fire conditions remain unverified.
No actual exemption, licence, preopening result or guaranteed duration is established; other company, staffing, supply and franchise-sales questions remain outside this scope.
editNote: Replaced two overlapping tables and repeated coffee exercises with the dated change, authority and project/opening consequences.
conditionsRetained: 16 July 2025 exact listed BSEED categories and retained Health licence.
Immediate-food-service versus retail/storage/manufacture authority boundary and mixed-operation facts.
289.6103 temporary/grocery conditions and deli/seating qualification; no licence exemption inference.
289.6105 complete accurate transmittal/fees and 289.6115 covered-work preopening conditions.
Local lead time and broader forms/premises source gaps unverified.

title: Whose tax residence matters—the owner’s or the company’s?
seoTitle: Owner nationality versus personal and company tax residence
description: An owner’s passport or UK address cannot answer every tax and immigration question. Identify the person, payment recipient and period first.
learningSummary: When a U.S. operator pays your foreign company, the owner’s nationality and home address do not establish the company’s treaty entitlement. Different questions test different people and facts.

sections.heading: Start with the person or recipient being tested
paragraphs: For a non-U.S.-citizen individual, IRS guidance generally uses green-card or substantial-presence tests, with elections, exceptions and treaty questions. That is not the same as company formation or the ultimate-owner nationality relevant to an immigration treaty.

For a payment, identify the actual company recipient and income. Company treaty residence, beneficial ownership and applicable limitation-on-benefits (LOB) conditions need their own facts; an owner’s personal residence does not establish them.

sections.heading: The UK treaty is an illustration, not a universal shortcut
paragraphs: Article 4 of the U.S.–UK treaty distinguishes individuals from other persons. For an individual treated as resident in both countries, earlier conditions—permanent home, closer personal/economic relationships and habitual abode—precede nationality in the described sequence. The person’s outcome cannot simply be copied onto the company.

A fictional owner living in the UK with another country’s citizenship and a company receiving U.S. royalties therefore has several questions, not one UK label. Establish the relevant person/entity and period under the actual law and treaty amendments. Keep identity and tax documents with their authorised private custodian.

practicalOutput: Identify the actual payment recipient and period before applying a personal-residence or nationality assumption to the company.
limitations: No day count, exception, residence result, treaty rate, payment entitlement or immigration approval is determined. The UK illustration does not define other treaties.
editNote: Removed the duplicated status worksheet and passport exercise; the replacement follows the actual recipient and the limited UK illustration.
conditionsRetained: Individual IRS tests with elections/exceptions/treaty issues.
Nationality, incorporation, personal and company residence are different questions.
Relevant payee/income, beneficial owner and LOB conditions.
UK Article 4 individual sequence and separate other-person rules; amendments matter.
No residence, tax-rate or immigration determination and private documents protected.

title: State payroll accounts: choose the employee’s work state
seoTitle: State payroll registration: withholding and unemployment accounts
description: Find the reviewed withholding and unemployment account routes for all 50 states and D.C., including state-specific timing and unresolved questions.
learningSummary: Choose the state or states where the employee will actually work. Have the legal employer, worker residence, work locations, first service and pay dates, and any ownership or business-acquisition facts ready.

sections.heading: Read the two account questions
paragraphs: Wage-income withholding is tax deducted from employee pay. Unemployment insurance (UI) has different employer coverage and reporting rules, even where one application serves both. An EIN or payroll-provider login does not create the state accounts.
Employee residence and applicable resident-state or local withholding can also matter. These entries do not supply a universal multi-state allocation rule.
bullets: Conditional: match the stated route to the actual employer and worker facts.
Unresolved or not researched: an answer is missing, not a finding that no duty applies.
Not applicable: only the specific wage-income withholding branch is closed.

sections.heading: Alabama
paragraphs: Give payroll the actual work-state and residence list. Keep the ALDOR account confirmation separate from the SR-2/UI determination rather than assuming one registration creates both.

rows: ALDOR directs employers with employees working in Alabama to obtain a withholding account through My Alabama Taxes. Its FAQ separately addresses Alabama residents working elsewhere, including withholding for the work state.
The Labor eGov Employer Registration service accepts Form SR-2 to determine SUI liability and obtain an account; a portal login is not itself a liability determination.

bullets: The eGov page contains older dated notices; only its identified registration function was relied on. UI thresholds, classification exceptions and current rates were not verified.

sections.heading: Alaska
paragraphs: For a foreign service company sending a crew to Alaska, identify who hires, directs and benefits from the work before choosing the reporting entity. Multi-state work needs a localization review rather than an automatic headquarters-state account.

rows: An Alaska personal-income-tax withholding conclusion was not established in this review. Do not infer the absence of other employee deductions or payroll obligations.

TaxWeb registers new businesses; the agency handbook requires UI accounts for workers hired and working in Alaska and says workers brought from elsewhere may also need reporting. The registration requests entity type and first wage date.

bullets: The retrieved handbook says last updated April 2024. This review uses its account/localization instructions, not annual contribution rates or a complete current exemption determination.

sections.heading: Arizona
paragraphs: A company that already holds an Arizona withholding account still needs the UI application route. Track each agency's determination instead of treating the joint form as a single approval.

rows: DES identifies the Joint Tax Application JT-1/UC-001 and an existing-withholding-account route, but the separate DOR withholding-obligations page returned HTTP 403. Withholding liability and sourcing remain unresolved.

Submit JT-1/UC-001 through DOR; DES uses it to decide UI liability and separately issues a determination stating the coverage start date, rate and eight-digit account number. The EIN is required for processing.

bullets: This records the DES process and separate review, not a conclusion that every Arizona business owes UI or withholding. DOR substantive withholding access remains blocked.

sections.heading: Arkansas
paragraphs: Do not substitute a federal UI threshold for Arkansas's stated ten-day ordinary-employer test. Assemble paid-work days, first wage date, ownership and acquisition facts before the Tax 21 session, which the agency says has no save option.

rows: The 2026 DFA instructions require withholding registration through AR-1R and identify ATAP online registration. They distinguish work in Arkansas from work outside it and allocate nonresident partly in-state services to Arkansas workdays.

The Reemployment agency uses Tax 21 and describes ordinary employer status after one or more workers perform services on ten or more days in a calendar year, plus acquisition, domestic, agricultural and voluntary-coverage categories.

bullets: Special employer categories have separate tests; the ten-day statement is not a universal threshold. The withholding PDF's employment-verification statements were not relied upon for federal I-9 rules.

sections.heading: California
paragraphs: Enroll the portal user, verify the email within EDD's stated 24-hour window, then submit the separate New Employer application. Preserve the eight-digit payroll account number; user enrollment alone does not create it.

rows: EDD registers employer payroll tax accounts through e-Services for Business and supplies distinct commercial, household, agricultural, nonprofit and other forms. Select the correct account category rather than treating incorporation as payroll enrollment.

EDD Step 1 requires a business that hires employees and pays more than $100 in wages in a calendar quarter to register within 15 days. Household employment has a separate $750 cash-wage threshold; use the appropriate account category.

bullets: Annual tax rates, wage bases, excluded employment, disability and paid-leave contributions require their own current review. Registration does not resolve worker classification.

sections.heading: Colorado
paragraphs: A foreign or other out-of-state employer should follow the CR 0100 branch rather than assuming the in-state portal route applies. Assign a separate owner to resolve CDLE unemployment registration.

rows: DOR requires a withholding-agent account when Colorado withholding is required. Its instructions distinguish in-state businesses using MyBizColorado or CR 0100 from out-of-state businesses using CR 0100; the account has no fee or renewal requirement.
The attempted CDLE registration page returned HTTP 403. The UI account procedure, liability thresholds and multi-state allocation were not substantively verified.

bullets: This establishes a conditional withholding-account process, not the underlying wage sourcing test, UI clearance or freedom from local occupational/payroll taxes.

sections.heading: Connecticut
paragraphs: Record both legal entity type and tax election before deciding whether an owner-manager's remuneration belongs in UI reports. An S corporation's federal income-tax treatment does not by itself exempt its paid officer's services from Connecticut UI.

rows: DRS links withholding to maintaining an office or transacting business in Connecticut and federal employer status, regardless of payroll department location. Register through myconneCT or add withholding to an existing DRS account.

DOL requires online ReEmployCT registration for employers of one or more people and separately describes liability thresholds. It expressly distinguishes sole proprietors, partners, paid corporate officers and LLC members according to relevant tax filing treatment.

bullets: The agency's LLC/officer discussion is Connecticut-specific. Family, nonprofit, domestic and other special coverage conditions still need fact-specific review.

sections.heading: Delaware
paragraphs: Map the employee's residence and actual work location before choosing full employer registration or withholding-agent-only treatment. Keep UC-1 submission and the resulting liability decision with the payroll file.

rows: One Stop distinguishes an employer conducting business in Delaware from an out-of-state business that may register as a withholding agent only for a Delaware resident as a courtesy. Do not turn that optional resident-service route into a universal duty.

One Stop directs businesses hiring one or more employees in Delaware to file UC-1 to determine unemployment liability and identifies withholding and workers' compensation as separate employer workstreams.

bullets: Only agency routing and the residence/work distinction were relied upon; older form names and broad withholding language on One Stop were not treated as complete current computation guidance.

sections.heading: Florida
paragraphs: Classify a service business as general, domestic, agricultural or another category before applying a threshold. Preserve the DR-1 determination; the guide treats corporate officers and LLC members differently according to the stated facts and tax classification.

rows: DOR expressly states Florida does not impose personal income tax. This closes only the state personal wage-income withholding branch; reemployment tax, corporate tax, sales tax and other payroll/business obligations remain separate.

DOR's reemployment guide requires DR-1 to determine liability; quarterly reports alone do not register an employer. It states general $1,500 quarterly wages, one employee in 20 weeks, or federal unemployment-tax liability tests, with separate special-employer categories.

bullets: The reemployment guide is revised March 2025; its annual rates were not relied on. The separate DOR tax guide supports the table’s narrow personal-income-tax statement. Worker classification and a complete current exclusion review remain outside this record.

sections.heading: Georgia
paragraphs: Put the first Georgia payroll date on the launch calendar and assign DOL-1A immediately afterwards. Keep payroll withholding and nonresident owner/distribution withholding as separate finance questions.

rows: DOR identifies employee-wage withholding, a separate registration-for-withholding-number route and Form G-4. Its page also covers other payment types, so a payroll number is not a determination of every nonresident-payment duty.

GDOL directs employing units with people performing services in Georgia to submit DOL-1A immediately after the first Georgia payroll. The FAQ separately states general liability and domestic/agricultural tests.

bullets: The DOR page contains a general rate description and the UI FAQ contains older wage-base text; neither was relied on as current rates or wage bases.

sections.heading: Hawaii
paragraphs: A Hawaii-based company sending staff outside the state cannot assume all wage withholding disappears. For UI, establish the owner's authorized account first and delegate the payroll provider through agency permissions.

rows: DOTAX states withholding applies to services in Hawaii and specified services outside it linked to the regular workplace or paying office. Obtain the WH account using BB-1 or add it in Hawaii Tax Online; the account has no opening fee.

The UI agency generally links tax to employees working in Hawaii and requires business owners to create the employer profile, after which they may authorize staff or service companies. Nonprofit, family-corporation and successor elections have separate conditions.

bullets: The withholding page contains inconsistent older return-form guidance; only its account and sourcing sections support this entry. Special UI elections are applications, not automatic exclusions.

sections.heading: Idaho
paragraphs: If a sole proprietorship becomes an LLC or a foreign buyer acquires operations, check the new-account branch. Using the predecessor's withholding voucher does not establish the buyer's own account.

rows: Obtain the EIN first, then use Idaho Business Registration. The Tax Commission says a withholding account is not transferable and requires a new account on business acquisition, a new EIN or a change of entity.

The Tax Commission's IBR guide routes businesses with employees to income-tax withholding and employee-related permits from Labor and the Industrial Commission. Prepare expected employee count, first paycheck and hire dates.

bullets: The separate UI handbook URL returned 404; IBR routing is verified, but Labor's substantive UI liability thresholds and localization are unresolved.

sections.heading: Illinois
paragraphs: Include a startup date and any purchase/reorganization in the payroll brief. The same portal can serve both agencies, but withholding registration and UI succession are different determinations.

rows: IDOR requires registration when Illinois withholding is mandatory or voluntarily undertaken and asks when Illinois payroll begins. MyTax Illinois/REG-1 handles registration; household employment has separate guidance.

IDES directs newly created employing units to register within 30 days of startup through MyTax Illinois or the liability form. A merger, acquisition or entity change has a separate succession/update workstream.

bullets: The 30-day statement is the agency's employing-unit registration rule, not a conclusion about every entity's tax liability. No current rate or full reciprocal-state analysis was performed.

sections.heading: Indiana
paragraphs: Record the actual Indiana work location and county before payroll setup. Creating an ESS user and obtaining the employer SUTA account are separate steps; use the agent route for a payroll provider.

rows: DOR directs employee businesses to collect state and county wage withholding, obtain an EIN and register through INBiz. It expressly points to county-specific rates rather than one statewide payroll setting.
DWD's Uplink ESS registration requires FEIN, legal name, NAICS, Indiana work location, first payroll date and responsible-party details; the SUTA number follows completed and approved registration.

bullets: This records account inputs and the existence of county withholding. It does not select an employee's county rate, settle reciprocity or verify every UI coverage exception.

sections.heading: Iowa
paragraphs: Treat a remote Iowa hire by a foreign or other out-of-state employer as a distinct registration event. Use a properly authorized agent account, not shared employer credentials, and confirm the applicable multi-state allocation before reporting.

rows: IDR links withholding to an office or business in Iowa, federal withholding and services performed in Iowa; obtain FEIN before Iowa registration. Residence and multi-state services still require the applicable sourcing review.

IWD says register through myIowaUI within 30 days of first Iowa wages or acquisition; out-of-state employers must register as soon as Iowa wages are paid. It separately discusses base-of-operations and direction/control for multi-state workers.

bullets: The agency page has a 2026 note changing out-of-state wage credits alongside older text; no wage-credit amount is asserted here. Account routing is not full employment-law coverage.

sections.heading: Kansas
paragraphs: Do not put a Kansas client's payroll under the reporting agent's own tax number. Identify resident versus nonresident workers and distinguish the employer's wage account from any owner-payment withholding.

rows: KDOR's KW-100 directs covered employers/payers to register through its Customer Service Center and separately addresses Kansas-resident and Kansas-work wages. It distinguishes wage withholding from nonresident-owner accounts and reporting-agent accounts.
The KDOL employer-services page returned HTTP 403; the current UI account route, timing and liability test were not substantively verified.

bullets: KW-100 displays revision 24.08. Its registration and account distinctions were reviewed, not current rates or a comprehensive 2026 wage-sourcing exception inventory.

sections.heading: Kentucky
paragraphs: Budget access to MyTaxes before payroll rather than assuming a paper-payment route. Assign a separate UI registration check and a local occupational-tax review for the employee's actual locality.

rows: DOR identifies resident/nonresident wage withholding subject to exemptions and directs registration, filing and payment through MyTaxes. Its 2026 instructions require electronic filing/payment for all employer filing frequencies.

The official employer page routes liable employers to an Employer Reserve Account, including acquisitions. The January 2026 KUIP FAQ says an account number and report filing are available immediately after completed registration.

bullets: The attempted UI-1 link returned non-substantive content; the separate official employer page and January 2026 KUIP FAQ were read. Liability thresholds, local occupational taxes and current rates remain separate.

sections.heading: Louisiana
paragraphs: Time account activation to the actual withholding start rather than opening it speculatively. Separately determine whether LAWATS needs a new employer account or access to an existing account, and preserve the agency's resulting status.

rows: LDR requires a withholding account before filing/remitting, but specifically warns not to register until Louisiana wage withholding begins. LaTAP registers a new business or adds an account; Secretary of State registration and EIN do not create it.

LWC's LAWATS login instructions require an existing seven-digit Employer Account Number and FEIN; a business without the EAN must apply for the unemployment tax account first. The owner then grants a third-party administrator access.

bullets: The LAWATS login guide is dated April 11, 2024. It distinguishes portal access from the tax account but does not establish current UI liability thresholds or sourcing exemptions.

sections.heading: Maine
paragraphs: A New Hampshire employer with a Maine resident should document work and business-location facts, not infer Maine withholding solely from residence or solely from headquarters. Preserve the distinction between mandatory and courtesy withholding.

rows: MRS's April 2026 FAQ routes new withholding accounts through the Maine Tax Portal and separately tests an out-of-state employer's Maine office/business, taxable payments and federal withholding. Courtesy withholding can differ from mandatory withholding.

The official ReEmployME guide distinguishes registration of a business without an EAN from creating access to an existing account. It states general and separate nonprofit/agricultural coverage tests and says a future date cannot be used to set up an account.

bullets: Official www1.maine.gov mirrors supplied the MRS FAQ and ReEmployME system guide after the main host blocked access. No annual rate, complete UI exclusion list or full remote-work sourcing determination is supplied.

sections.heading: Maryland
paragraphs: Record remuneration to a paid officer and the actual employing entity before labeling a small company 'owner only.' After BEACON, obtain a separate Comptroller withholding answer rather than treating UI enrollment as all tax registration.

rows: The 2026 Comptroller guide requires CRA registration and a Central Registration Number, warns not to wait until withholding is due, and says an acquirer must not use the seller's number. The September 2026 CRA guide routes applications through Maryland Tax Connect.

Labor requires an employer UI account through BEACON, distinguishes covered from excluded work and expressly includes paid corporate officers in covered employment. Other tax registration and UI are separate.

bullets: Withholding and UI registration are separate from Maryland FAMLI, local withholding computations, worker exclusions and full wage sourcing. No annual rate or paid-leave date is asserted.

sections.heading: Massachusetts
paragraphs: A short Massachusetts assignment by an out-of-state company deserves its own UI review; do not automatically substitute a familiar $1,500 threshold from another category or state. Distinguish proprietor income from wages to an employee.

rows: DOR's August 2026 guide distinguishes resident and nonresident wages and directs employers to register before filing/payment through MassTaxConnect. A sole proprietor is generally not an employee solely for paying their own personal tax.

DUA lists general contribution tests and distinct domestic/agricultural categories; it specifically states an out-of-state employer test of $200 gross Massachusetts wages in a quarter. Its account route is Unemployment Services for Employers.

bullets: The $200 statement is the agency's out-of-state-employer category, not a universal tax-free allowance or a withholding threshold. No annual rates or full sourcing exceptions are supplied.

sections.heading: Michigan
paragraphs: Confirm the current MiUI workflow rather than reusing an old payroll-provider checklist. Keep the employer's own access and authorize the third party through the agency route; a provider's login is not the employer's registration evidence.

rows: Treasury's MTO business-tax eRegistration process and separate user/business-account linkage were read, but that general page does not establish withholding liability, sourcing or account-selection criteria. Those remain unresolved.

UIA's current help center says MiUI is live for all tax/benefit functions and employers should hold their own MiUI account even when using a third-party administrator. It separately routes business registration and account authorization.

bullets: The reviewed Treasury page covers business registration generally; withholding liability and sourcing require a separate substantive tax analysis. No broad Michigan tax clearance is implied.

sections.heading: Minnesota
paragraphs: Minnesota's withholding and UI account timing differ: prepare withholding before deductions, but do not preregister UI before covered wages are actually paid. Retain both numbers and resolve owner/officer coverage before selecting wage records.

rows: DOR's new-employer guide requires a Minnesota ID and withholding account before tax is withheld. It distinguishes that number from DEED's UI account used for state unemployment reporting.

The UI handbook says register after covered wages have actually been paid and before the first required quarterly wage-detail report is due. It asks entity type, owner/officer interests, Minnesota work dates and acquisition facts, with special categories treated separately.

bullets: Covered employment, owner/officer elections, nonprofit and other special categories still require their own tests. This is not a Paid Leave registration or full employment-law determination.

sections.heading: Mississippi
paragraphs: A recruitment-platform registration does not activate unemployment reporting. For an acquisition, tell DOR the ownership/entity facts and retain the correct acquiring-employer account before the first post-acquisition payroll.

rows: DOR requires a withholding account for employers subject to Mississippi withholding, with online application through TAP. Its instructions require acquisition/entity changes to be assessed rather than using the predecessor's addressed return.

MDES separates employment-service registration from the New Business unemployment-tax registration, and separately offers online access for an already assigned account. An employer needing both service categories must register for both.

bullets: This does not establish UI liability thresholds or all resident/nonresident sourcing rules. No annual withholding/UI rate is supplied.

sections.heading: Missouri
paragraphs: Keep the legal entity filing, DOR withholding number and UI liability outcome as three records. A foreign company temporarily sending a team should also investigate the transient-employer category before assuming ordinary registration is sufficient.

rows: DOR's 2026 guide directs employers paying wages to employees working in Missouri to register online or using Form 2643. The permanent withholding number is not transferable; transient-employer requirements are a separate category.

Labor's new-employer guide distinguishes Secretary of State formation from DOR tax registration and directs the employer to a separate UI liability review. New liable employers receive an industrial classification for UI.

bullets: The Labor checklist is an official route to the separate liability process, not a complete UI threshold finding. Transient-employer security amounts and exemptions remain unresolved.

sections.heading: Montana
paragraphs: A zero-withholding W-2 does not by itself remove the account question described by Montana DOR. Put the Montana work-start date and the legal employer's IRS-matching name into the application brief.

rows: DOR requires a withholding account when a business issues Montana wages, W-2s with or without withholding, or 1099s with withholding. Apply through TAP or GenReg with FEIN and the date employees started Montana work.

DLI's UI eServices is the named employer registration/reporting portal, with separate UI Contributions Bureau assistance. The page establishes the account route, not the coverage or localization test.

bullets: No UI threshold, worker exclusion, tax rate or multi-state allocation is established by the portal overview. Other state payroll deductions remain separate.

sections.heading: Nebraska
paragraphs: Obtain the employer's own withholding certificate before the provider files. At the year change, use the correctly dated Circular EN: the official page separates tables through December 31, 2026 from those starting January 1, 2027.

rows: DOR requires Form 20 and a Nebraska withholding number before state deductions. The employer remains responsible for the application when using a payroll service; provide that service the issued Withholding Certificate.

Nebraska One Stop identifies the DOL unemployment tax-account application, but its short listing supplies no thresholds or complete instructions. Substantive coverage and registration inputs remain open.

bullets: The FAQ retains older rate and pandemic passages; those are not relied on. Current numeric rates and UI liability are not established here.

sections.heading: Nevada
paragraphs: Do not substitute another state's $1,500 general threshold for Nevada's stated $225 test. Record the Nevada work and wage facts and request the actual account/coverage decision, including any excluded-employment question.

rows: Nevada Constitution Article 10,section 1(9) prohibits income tax on natural persons' wages/personal income while permitting business-income/revenue taxes. Personal wage-income withholding is therefore distinct from UI, Modified Business Tax and other business taxes.

DETR says generally an employing unit paying $225 or more for Nevada employment in a calendar quarter must register with Employment Security and pay UI tax. Its employing-unit definition includes entities and individuals.

bullets: The $225 statement is a general UI coverage rule, not a tax-free allowance or an MBT/other-tax conclusion. Annual rates and all exceptions were not reviewed.

sections.heading: New Hampshire
paragraphs: A transfer of a New Hampshire workforce is itself a reporting event. Assemble predecessor, assets, trade/workforce and entity details rather than limiting the registration brief to the first wage amount.

rows: NH Economy's state economic-development guidance states there is no state income tax in its salary/cost-of-living context. This is limited to personal wage-income withholding; business-profits and business-enterprise taxes and other employer duties remain separate.

Emp 303.01, amended effective June 26, 2026, requires an Employer Status Report within 30 days of furnishing employment, becoming an employer, specified status changes or business/workforce transfers. It requests entity, NH work and wage dates, locations and acquisition facts.

bullets: The operative current rule was read from the official administrative-code text; the NHES agency handbook download was blocked. Portal steps, underlying statutory coverage and all exceptions need separate confirmation.

sections.heading: New Jersey
paragraphs: For a Pennsylvania resident, retain the required reciprocity certificate rather than assuming residence alone stops NJ withholding. Separately evaluate UI and other contributions; an income-tax reciprocal rule does not settle those duties or Pennsylvania local wage taxes.

rows: NJ-WT requires FEIN and, for a corporate entity, the state's ten-digit corporate ID for registration. It distinguishes resident/nonresident work, Pennsylvania reciprocity certificates and certain convenience-of-employer sourcing.

Employer Accounts directs NJ-REG first and describes employer status after one or more workers and $1,000 annual wages, with automatic coverage for FUTA-subject employing units. UI, disability and family-leave contributions are named separately.

bullets: NJ-WT is marked September 2025. No full convenience-rule, reciprocity, worker-classification or annual-rate determination is made. Historical case excerpts on the UI page are not treated as independently reviewed court decisions.

sections.heading: New Mexico
